name: create-partition-trusted
description: A partition created whole already `trusted`. No address arm reads a `hardware` create; the guard compares two models and reads a partition the baseline lacks as the default class, `non_trusted`, so creating one trusted is the same grant as making an existing one trusted, and it is asked about exactly the same way.

context.summary: The `examples/basic` model as it stands: `PARTITION0` is the one partition, unrated and `non_trusted`, on the unrated `CORE0`. The change set creates `PARTITION1` on `CORE0`, unrated and `trusted`. No partition declares a level, so neither trust rule fires on the staged model.

authorization.notes: The scope covers the created element exactly. It does not authorize the safety question: the partition arrives `trusted`, which the guard decides by comparing two models, so `grant_partition_trust` is asked once for the whole change set and the status is `committed`.

input.intent: Add a trusted partition on CORE0.

value.name: PARTITION1
value.description: A second partition on CORE0, trusted and unrated, running nothing yet.

after.name: PARTITION1
after.description: A second partition on CORE0, trusted and unrated, running nothing yet.

expected.notes: `committed` after the second question. A trusted partition beside a rated one would be judged by the two trust rules — below the highest level, or unrated beside a level above `QM` — and pass D would refuse it; here nothing is rated, so the act is legal and it is the grant itself that the human answers for.
